headline: PM hands over appointment letters to three persons with disabilities
summary: The recipients, including two women who completed their master's degrees by writing with their feet, have been appointed to various government roles.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman handed over appointment letters to three persons with disabilities at his office in the Cabinet Division at the secretariat today.
The initiative is part of the government's efforts to promote economic empowerment and inclusion of persons with disabilities in the mainstream of society.

Neela Khatun from Sirajganj, who was born without both hands and completed her master's degree by writing with her feet, has been appointed as a teacher at the National Foundation for the Development of the Disabled in Mirpur, Dhaka.
Ayesha Akter from Gaibandha, who also completed her master's degree by writing with her feet and has no hands, received her appointment letter using her mouth.
Ayesha has been appointed as a class supervisor at BIAM Laboratory School and College in Gaibandha.
Visually impaired Md Hasmat Ali from Narail Sadar has been appointed as a Union Social Worker under the Department of Social Services.
The event was attended by the Social Welfare and Women and Children Affairs Adviser Prof Dr AZM Zahid Hossain and State Minister for Women and Children Affairs Farzana Sharmin Putul.
Abdus Sattar Dulal, founder of the Bangladesh Protibondhi Kalyan Somity, later met the prime minister to express gratitude for the providing jobs to the three individuals.

headline_marked: Govt to maintain [[zero-tolerance policy against human trafficking]] and cyber scams
headline: Govt to maintain zero-tolerance policy against human trafficking and cyber scams
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed warns that criminal networks are using fake online recruitment to lure jobseekers into forced criminality.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced a zero-tolerance policy against international human trafficking and cyber scam networks. He spoke at a national dialogue titled 'Trapped Behind the Scam: Ending Human Trafficking for Forced Criminality' in Dhaka.

The minister warned that criminal networks are increasingly using fake online recruitment platforms and social media to target young people and jobseekers with false promises of lucrative jobs abroad.
Victims are often confined in cyber scam centres where they are subjected to torture and intimidation and forced to engage in criminal activities, the minister said.

To combat this, the government has introduced the Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Prevention and Suppression Act, 2026, which includes tougher penalties for online scams and technology-driven deception.

The government is also updating the Human Trafficking Prevention and Suppression Rules, 2017, and finalizing a National Action Plan 2026-2030 focusing on prevention, protection, prosecution, and partnership.
A digital anti-trafficking information management platform is being developed to improve data-driven policymaking and case tracking.
The minister emphasized that protecting the dignity and rehabilitation of survivors is a moral and legal responsibility of the government.
He urged the media and civil society to raise public awareness about safe migration and fraudulent recruitment, especially among women and young people.
